svg.title: Fabric Delivery Phase Gates: Environments, CI/CD, Testing, Security, Operational Readiness
svg.desc: An original decision-tree infographic tracing five sequential delivery-phase gates for a Fabric implementation. Gate 1 asks whether Dev, Test, and Production workspaces with Git integration exist; failing routes back to environment setup. Gate 2 asks whether Deployment Pipelines promote items with Variable Library environment binding and a pull-request gate; failing routes back to CI/CD wiring. Gate 3 asks whether pipeline reliability and idempotency are tested; failing routes back to hardening retries and Delta MERGE writes. Gate 4 asks whether secrets, identities, and permissions follow least privilege; failing routes back to security remediation. Gate 5 asks whether recovery, monitoring, and support ownership are proven; only then does the pattern reach general availability. A feedback edge shows drift discovered in production returning to the environments gate. A legend distinguishes fact, pattern, and warning classifications and flow versus branch versus feedback edges.
svg.text: Fabric delivery phase gates — environments to operational readiness
Five sequential gates a Fabric implementation must clear: environments · CI/CD (Deployment Pipelines) · testing · security · operational readiness
A failed gate routes back to the phase that must be hardened — the pattern advances only with evidence, not confidence.
DECISION PATH · READ LEFT TO RIGHT · EACH GATE MUST PASS BEFORE THE NEXT OPENS

g.aria-label: Gate 1 — do isolated Dev, Test, and Production workspaces exist with Git integration?
g.title: Gate 1 — Environments: are Dev, Test, and Production workspaces isolated and Git-integrated?

g.aria-label: Gate 2 — do Deployment Pipelines promote items with environment-specific configuration and a pull-request gate?
g.title: Gate 2 — CI/CD: do Deployment Pipelines promote items with Variable Library binding and a PR gate before production?

g.aria-label: Gate 3 — is pipeline reliability tested with retries and idempotent writes?
g.title: Gate 3 — Testing: is failure handling exercised — retries with backoff, and idempotent Delta MERGE writes?

g.aria-label: Gate 4 — do secrets, identities, and permissions follow least privilege?
g.title: Gate 4 — Security: are secrets vaulted, identities service-based, and permissions scoped to least privilege?

g.aria-label: Gate 5 — is recovery, monitoring, and support ownership proven before general availability?
g.title: Gate 5 — Operational readiness: is item recovery tested and is a support owner proven before go-live?

g.aria-label: Remediation loop — a failed gate routes back into the same phase for hardening
g.title: Remediation loop — a failed gate routes back into the same phase for hardening rather than proceeding with a gap.
g.text: NO → remediate this phase and re-enter the same gate; do not advance a workload past an unmet gate

g.aria-label: Feedback — configuration drift found in production returns to the environments gate
g.title: Feedback — configuration drift discovered in production re-opens Gate 1 rather than being patched in place.

g.text: Risk: dev creds reused as prod identity
Risk: promotion with no PR gate

svg.text: Every gate governs the same shared platform
Workspaces, capacity, Git, and identity are tenant-wide constructs — a gate passed once in Dev must be re-proven, not assumed, in Prod.
DECISION PRINCIPLE · Advance a Fabric implementation gate by gate — a workspace that skips testing or security to hit a go-live date is not ahead, it is unmeasured.
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; item icons vendored under Microsoft's Fabric icon terms.
